Each is a real ES module with a real public export table, each already had a reading copy under readable/, and each had NO derived text to compare against: the vendor rule keeps those chunks whole and unsliced, so they have no src/ slice, and the section pointed at an index-only name ('vendor/...') that is not a file. Each vendor whole-file section now names the READING COPY in `file` and the SERVED CHUNK in `origin`, and carries no `capture` field - a `capture` field makes the gate compare the served chunk with itself. The pristine is therefore the served file, so the comparison is live: PROOF, in a throwaway copy outside D:/repos/mirrors, renaming the public export of the served chunk assets/auto-CBo2XcXh.js (export{Nl as t} -> export{Nl as tMutated}) turns the gate RED and names the lost public name - 'wholefile:assets/auto-CBo2XcXh.js: a public export name was LOST: tMutated', with 'the capture exported: tMutated' and 'the layer exports: t', exit 1. The two sides are two different files (the served chunk and its reading copy), so no table is compared with itself. The nine tables still uncovered are the READING COPIES' own instances of those same tables: a reading copy of a whole-file vendor chunk has no other derived text in this mirror (it is never sliced and the vendor rule keeps it out of src/), and the gate refuses to compare a file with itself.
